entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Nanqal

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage 38171 (10571 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We stayed at the Youth Hostel; we ate out there. I had sweet and sour chicken and rice. The rice wasn’t very nice. In the morning we had to go and get some “third-party insurance”, when we had got it, we drove on towards Bhakra Dam.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We saw a wedding procession. First were four men carrying a litter with the bride in it, then were a few people, some with musical instruments, and then a horse with the bridegroom riding on it, and then were some tag-enders. It was quite a small get-up, but very gay and colourful.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove through some beautiful hills; there were quite a few different kinds of cacti. From some bits of the road we could see the snow-covered Himalayas.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We drove from Amritsar to Mangal.  On the way we went through some very green hills.  We went through lots of cut places.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 38254 (10654 miles travelled).  Ropar

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the morning, we set out for Bhakra Dam. We had to stop at the Public Relations office, because a sign said we had to get a permit to see the dam. In the end, we had to take a man with us. The drive was through the foothills of the Himalayas, there were lots of signs, with things like “Safety Saves”, etc. When we got to the Dam, water wasn’t pouring through at the top, so it wasn’t as impressive as it might have been. We left the man there and drove up to the top of the dam, the scenery was lovely. We drove back to Nangal and bought some dal (lentils) for lunch and a curry and some chapatis. Dad bought some Cashew nuts, mmm!

entries.speaker: F
entries.text:
We went to the Bhakra Dam. There were some very steep cuttings through the hills. We drove along up a road. We were stopped at a checkpoint. It took a lot of paperwork to get through it.
[PIC]

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: A public relations officer there [explained that there were] five big Dynamos each generating 90,000 kilowatts. There was a big crane on an overhead trolley. It was lifting a big oil drum. There was also an interesting flying fox across the river lower down. It had no supports for a very long distance. You could see big logs on the trolleys.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Then we drove on to Chandigarh. On the way we saw some bullocks working a well.  We also saw two vultures.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: On the way to Chandigarh we saw some bullocks working a wheel, which was turning a horizontal axle, which worked another wheel and bucket chains. The water flowed from a bucket chain to a tin channel. The water was flowing faster than I expected.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We visited Bakhra Dam, we had to wait a long time at a checkpost while they looked at all our passports.  The clerk wrote down the number of our Afghan visas as he said we should have a visa.  The dam was big and ugly.  The surrounding hills were beautiful and very green.  The dam was 740 feet high, it had 4 flood gates near the top, also at the bottom there were quite a lot of pipes with water coming out.  The water was very green from the reflection of the hills, the water flow was very fast.  On the way to Chandigarh, we saw a water wheel - two bullocks made it work.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We left Chandigar on the long drive to Simla. On the way we stopped at the Pinjor Gardens; they were beautiful. There was a mini-zoo. I crossed the safety barrier to look at the Lesser Pandas. I walked too close to the Rhesus Monkey cage and the big male put out his hand and grabbed Mum’s bag. I backed away, and then made a grab at the bag. I got it, but the strap ripped. I was terrified.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the afternoon, we started climbing. We were just driving into the Pinewood Inn when David and a friend cycled up. We had drinks with them. We then drove on, until we had to stop behind a long queue of other vehicles. We went to see what had happened; a big bit of mountain had collapsed onto the road.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: They had a big bulldozer, which was trying to shift all the rubble, but there were some huge boulders that had to be blasted with dynamite. It really made me jump. They also had men with crowbars pushing down rocks. It was very frightening to watch them. I thought all the time that someone was going to go over the edge. We just slept where we were, in Fred. There was a beautiful sunset, with all the colours merging and tinting the clouds. At 1:00 in the morning they got through. But I slept through it all.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We were visiting Simla when we were stopped by a traffic jam. We went forward and found that some rocks had fallen [across the road]. There was a bulldozer, but there were some rocks bigger than it; in the end they blasted it. There were two big booms, and when we came back some of the rock had all split up. The driver was very clever: he dug under and pushed it over the edge. The rocks looked lovely as they rolled over the edge and down the slope. One rock got the edges chipped to a circle so that it was like a big stone wheel. One man nearly fell down. They didn’t shift the rocks so we stayed the night.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We visited the beautiful mogul gardens of Pinjore; the outside looked like a fort - it had some lovely decorations.  The arrow-slits looked quite nice.  When we went in, F and I went straight to the bottom garden (there were seven gardens).  In the third, there was a zoo in it.  There were monkeys, birds, porcupines and a few of the dog family.  The only monkeys I can remember there were pig-tailed monkeys and the lesser pandas.  We stayed for a very long time at the peacocks gathering feathers.  We found one of the feathers on the peacock.  We also got some good ones from the peahen.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 38369 (10769 miles travelled).  Simla

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We woke up to find the road was clear. We packed up ready to drive, resolving to have breakfast at Simla. When we got there, we couldn’t find the Mall, and we seemed to go on and on through beautiful mountain scenery, coming to little hamlets and viewpoints. At length, we stopped by the side of the road and, crossing a fence, went for a walk. There were quite a few private houses, they were all very deserted though. In one, I saw some horse-drawn carriages through one window. We went back to Fred and some Indians on a motor scooter told us then in one kilometre was a super rest house place. We drove there; it was nice. There was a nice garden and some super views. We stayed the night and ate out there.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: At 1 o’clock (am) they cleared the road. We rested until 7am and went to Simla. In a bazaar we got some chapatis stuffed with vegetable curry.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to some pine woods. There were some lovely crickets but they weren’t chirping. One was rather small and had very heavy camouflage, but had red on the back legs. Dad heard a woodpecker, but we didn’t see it. We camped at a dak bungalow and lazed around. H and I went for a walk. On the way back we saw some monkeys in the trees and one big one on the ground. I think they were Rhesus monkeys because they were big. We ran all the way to Fred. There was a nice man at the dak bungalow. There was a lovely view of forestry mountains, a small plain and snowy mountains beyond.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We had had to spend the night on the road because of a landslip after dynamiting.  In the morning, the road had been cleared so we drove straight to Simla.  At Simla, we got lost and did some shopping.  At last after breakfast, which was porridge, we found a path going into some woods.  We followed it up a hill where there was a grassy glade.  There was a small hollow full of small fluffy feathers.  It looked as though a bird had been eaten there.  Soon we came to an abandoned house and heard a woodpecker.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We had buttered toast. We all went for a walk. We found lots of interesting new plants. Some of them were very green. Dad and I plaited with them. We saw some very shaggy ponies, with a boy looking after them. When I was hanging up the washing I found a peg. I made it into a lady. She had matchstick arms and I made hair from some wool from my sheepskin.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: This morning very early, Mum went for a walk to look at the sunrise. She saw it and some monkeys; they were climbing on an old shed. Then we went for a walk. At first we went on the road, but we turned off at a pond. There were some lovely horses and ponies. The ponies had lovely shaggy coats. We went up to an old, abandoned tennis court. There were some lovely lichens. I thought they would make super miniature soldier bushes if they were painted. We plaited some broom plant into a rope then came back.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: When we woke up in the morning, we cuddled for an hour.  At 8 o’clock we were served hot buttered toast and chipatys (sic).  We went for a walk by a big pool.  We saw several ponies.  Three of them were small and shaggy. (Pic)  We walked up the hill and discovered an old tennis court.  We went on a prickly path - it soon widened and we sat down in the sun.  Daddy and Denise plaited some strong green plant things.  Mum says there(sic) broom.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We had hot buttered toast served to us in Fred again. When we were ready to go, Baljeet told me to come with him, as he had a present for me. He gave me a pendant on a nice chain, and some “marriage bangles” [PIC]. Then we left to go to Pinjore. By the time we had come down the interesting drive from the mountains it was dusk. All the fountains were playing and everything was beautifully illuminated. We hired a suite. The garden was composed of seven terraces. On the two two were some nice Moghul buildings. We had a suite in the first building. The beds were the original ones that the Maharaja and Maharani slept in (the ones who owned the gardens). We had dinner at the restaurant there, and morning tea at 7:30, drove to Delhi, arrived 3:30. [PIC]

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We left Simla. The nice man gave D a necklace with a big jewel in a hexagonal thing.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: It was a long drive to the Pinjore Gardens, but we finally reached them. On the way, we passed some trucks carrying mules. The mules were very like horses. We got a suite. It was built by the moguls. Inside there were some lovely carved wood ceilings with mirrors on them. At the bottom of the gardens, there was a zoo. At the monkey cage there were some big rhesus monkeys. Outside, there were some little rabbits suckling on their mum. All the fountains were lit up and some of the trees were illuminated. I liked a big red fountain most.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We left Simla and went to the Pinjore gardens.  In the end we stayed there at a suite.  The gardens and even the beds ventured back to the times of Maharajahs and Mahareenas though the rest of the furniture was modern.  Maharajahs and Mahareenas were only about 300 years ago.  In the zoo, F and I found lots of budgerigar feathers.  We also found six really big ones.  My favourite feather is grey fluff until about half way then it goes black and white stripes then a dollop of brown surrounded by green which shines gold in the light.  When we went, the fountains were playing and all the lights were on.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 38521 (10921 miles travelled).  Chatt. Lake

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We had lunch at a kind of sweet meat snack bar. We had “Masa Dosa” for the first time; it was a long, crunchy stuffed pancake. I didn’t like the stuffing. After lunch, we parked Fred and walked down a street full of wood and ivory and little things. There were also lots of cotton skirts and cheesecloth blouses, etc. I bought a nose ring, one that didn’t need a hole. Mum bought a lovely long skirt. H bought a fan made of peacock feathers, and a very small ivory elephant.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to the poste restante. I got the only letter; it was from Adam. He has got some German paratroopers, and is now Golden Arrow in Cubs. On the first of November he got a black eye in a fight. I am missing Adam a lot.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to some shops in Janpath. They had some very clever hanging things made out of string. They could fold very small. Some had some nice woollen embroidery on them. Helena thought they were light shades. In a big emporium there were some nice wooden elephants with ivory tusks. Helena liked a huge elephant bigger than her. It was stuffed. I liked a big wooden chess set, but it cost the earth. Mummy got a big cotton skirt with animals on. It had some lovely colours.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the evening we caught a little motor cab and went to the Red City to see the Son et Lumière, but we were too late, as we had been on summer timing, not winter. It was really fun going on the cabs though.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: In the campsite at Delhi, F and I chased chipmunks.  One ate from F’s hand, lots of others ate cottonwool from the ground where we had put it - we had put some on the ground.  We drove to the poste restante where F found a letter from Adam.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: In the afternoon, we went shopping in Janpath Marg(?), quite a few of the shops had fans made from peacocks.  You could get long tail feathers or a small round one with eyes round the outside and a flower of them in the middle.  F and I found some real ivory elephants, there were some small ones for 5 rupees, one was very nicely carved and I bought it for 4 rupees.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: For lunch, we were walking around, and we saw a block which was entirely made of cramped little eating places.  We had lunch there.  My Dal was very hot. After lunch we walked to the Friday Mosque. It was very like the one at Lahore. We climbed one minaret and had a view of Delhi, under its smog. We came out of the mosque and rushed to the circus. We bought the most expensive seats – 5 rupees (35p) – and watched the lions and tigers getting ready. Some of the children were very good, and there was one youngish elephant who played getting drunk. He was really good. There was also an orangutang, who looked just like Steptoe.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We climbed through two barbed wire fences. There was quite a nice little park but we couldn’t stop. We went to a little food place. I had a nice mutton curry with rice. We went to the Friday mosque; it was very like the one at Lahore. From the minaret you could see the Big Top and the Red Fort. From the minaret all you could see were trees, in the Red Fort. We walked on to the circus. When we went in they had the lions getting ready. I liked the tigers; they looked even nicer than I thought. Their teeth looked terrifying.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We had lunch at a roadside stall.  I had fried chipatties and the others had curries.  Then we walked to the Friday Mosque which was very like the great Mosque in Lahore.  We climbed up a Minaret, it was rather dark; we could see the Big Top.  The Circus had lots of horses, a zebra, two deer, ten elephants, five camels, a hippopotamus etc.  I had expected to see the horses but we only saw them three times.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: While Mum and Dad were doing boring things, F, H & I went shopping. F bought a lovely little elephant, I found some “Sangam spots” [to mark your “third eye”] and some toe rings with bells on. When we got back, quite late, to the campsite, there was a letter from Franjit and Prenna, inviting us to a party. We quickly put on some good clothes and drove off. We left F & H at their house. It was Shashees birthday party. We really made pigs of ourselves; it was super.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 38653 (11053 miles travelled).  Delhi

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: [On the way home] a jackal ran across the road. We saw some vultures. We got back at about 1:30am and just flopped into bed.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: At 6:00am, Dad was sick. By mistake he spilt cold water all down my back.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We met Nipinder Singh (Nippy) and his wife at the party, and we went and had a picnic with them on their uncle’s farm. After we had eaten, we went to visit something on the way back. It was the Qutab Minar”, a very beautiful Mughul building. It was very different from the other mosques we’d been seeing; it was much more open than some of the others.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: When we got home, I tried on a sari, and a punjab costume. We had dinner and then went to where we had the party. They had some spare rooms we could use, and they said to ask the servant for anything we wanted. [PIC OF SARI AND PUNJAB COSTUME ON 3 DEC]

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We went shopping with Ranjit and Prenna, and Nippy. We bought 15 towels. Prenna kept on saying, “Buy some more, buy some more.”

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Prenna has 300 saris, most of them given to her on her wedding. She showed us lots of photos of her wedding. It had been a typical southern wedding with lots of interesting customs.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We looked around emporiums. In the Nagaband emporium there were some crossbows. [PIC] It was an ordinary bow with some wood fitted on. It had a hole to hold. You pulled it back into a dip with a bit of wood on. This came through like a trigger when you pulled it, released the string and shot a bolt. There were some nice spears with red on, and some hats that had the tip of an elephant’s tusk. The most ferocious things were knives. They had a strange shape: a broad blade narrowing to the handle.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We had a late breakfast and went and bought D a sari.  Previna came and advised us.  Soon afterwards we went to look at the State Emporiums.  There were lots of brass figures, especially of their gods.  There were hundreds of saris and many shawls, bedspreads etc.  In one ship, Mummy bought me a skirt with mirrors on the tie belt and a matching top with 4 bells on.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the morning, we went shopping with Prenna, to buy my sari. It was very difficult choosing, but at last we found one that draped nicely, and had quite a nice Indianish pattern. Then we went and looked around the state emporiums. I bought some presents for friends.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 38771 (11171 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the morning we went round all the little shops, along Jan path. In the afternoon we went to the sailing club with Ranjit & Prenna, and Nippy. There was a race. Ranjit came fifth. We went in a motor boat and cheered him on, etc. We had dinner with Mrs Pai (Prenna’s Mum). I wore my sari. By the end of the evening it was all uneven and I had lost most of the tucks.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 38926 (11326 miles travelled) outside Agra

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We left Delhi. On the way we looked at the poste restante. There was a letter from Sarah!

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We packed up and got some gas. Then we went to the poste restante. Denise got a letter from Sarah Woodam. Then we left.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: On the way to Agra we saw some Sarus cranes; they had lovely red crests. When we reached Agra we looked for a campsite. One had a guard; he had a bayonet and a red uniform.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We got to Agra quite late. There was a full moon, but it was very misty. We found a campsite, we had to use the loos in the little rooms. The first one wasn’t clean; the next didn’t work and had no paper; at last we got one. Then we went to see the Taj. It was very misty and the marble gleamed dully in the moonlight. It was very spooky.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: The moon was full, so we went to look at the Taj Mahal. Unluckily there was lots of mist. The Taj wasn’t what I had expected. I had thought it would be bigger and have gold, not inlays. The inlays were nice: one small flower had 30 pieces! In the mist the Taj looked like a ghost.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Inside the Taj there was a big area fenced with lattice. In there, there were two tombs.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the Taj were two beautifully inlaid tombs. There was a downstairs, and there were two other tombs, also beautifully inlaid, exactly underneath the other tombs. Seven feet below these, Shah Jahan and his wife were actually buried. This had been worked out so that no-one could step over their graves.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We packed up and went to get some gas.  Afterwards we drove to Agra.  Once there, we drove along the river and at last found a Hotel where we stayed for ten rupees.  As it was the night of the full moon, we went to see the Taj Mahal by moonlight.  The Taj Mahal is a memorial to Shah Jhahan’s wife.  It is built of white marble and sandstone with lots of inlays of flowers and trees.  It is very famous.  There are two tombs, two in one floor and two in a room below.  The bodies are seven feet below the bottom tombs.  It was rather echoee (sic) in the top tombs but below was nice and quiet.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text:
In the morning we saw the “Itmad-ud-daulah”. Its gardens went right down to the river. We saw lots of bullocks, and people doing their washing in the river.
We also went to see the Agra Fort. There was a big basin, 4 feet deep, carved out of one big block of stone. It was a bath. In another part of the fort we saw the “favourite wife’s” bathroom. It has a cold bath, hot bath, and perfumed bath. The whole room was mirrored; it was beautiful. We saw two pure marble mosques. They were very bright in the sunlight. It was a very proper fort: portcullis, drawbridge, moat full of crocodiles, and boiling oil. Some of the palaces were very beautiful.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We got up late and had the first porridge since Simla, then we went to a tomb. It had some styles like those in the Taj Mahal. I liked the beautiful paintings of trees and roses. We went to a cheap wayside place to eat. But alas it was hot, really hot. I could have burnt.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text:
Then we went to Agra Fort. There were lots of brilliant defence systems. Each gate had two walls fixed on the big one. In a courtyard there were some men cutting grass with swords. We went on to a palace. It had some nice sandstone lattices with all kinds of shapes. Some of the balconies had nicely carved serpents on them. (pic)
We got up late and went to see another memorial.  There were two tombs in every room.  After that, we went to Agra Fort.  F and I went and climbed in the battlements, it was made of red sandstone.  Opposite the Jahangir Palace was the giant bath.  We visited a palace with very elabrat (sic) and pretty carvings but I preferred the other walls.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We got a guide and went round the Taj again. It was very different in the daylight. The guide showed us some very interesting optical illusions [SEE 3RD W]

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: When we had seen the Taj, we drove to Fatehpur Sikri. Just before we left Agra I bought some chappals (sandals).

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Fatehpur Sikri was an enormous Mughal City built by Akbar, in 1569 AD; 14 years later – it’s said because the water supply failed – [the city was abandoned]. There were some beautiful buildings. Almost the whole place was built of red sandstone. The place, as a whole, was very well preserved.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We visited the Taj. It had some nice inlays [PIC 1]. The carnelian one, if you put a torch on one end the other lit up. There were some nice carvings of flowers and trees round the bottom. The top of the big dome had a brass shape on [PIC 2].

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: When we left, we went to the shops. There were some lovely little models of the Taj, which you put lights in and they glowed. Then we got a Ganesh. He had an elephant’s head and four arms; the turban was white. In two of his hands he had weapons; the other two were held out. I think he looked nice. We also got two small elephants to go with Ganesh. Then we went to Fatehpur Sikri.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went to see the Taj Mahal.  I thought the atmosphere in the daytime is nicer than in the evening, it had been very misty.  The guide showed us some flowers made of carnelian - they glowed red when lit up.  We went to a shop where F and I found a lovely Ganesh carved out of soapstone.  We bought two ELEFANTS (sic) to be his bodyguards.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the morning we looked around Fatehpur Sikri properly. There was a big water tank, lots of people were offering to jump in from the walls, for money. The walls were c.100 feet high, and the tank about 30 feet deep. We saw some very original-looking holy men, with dyed beards, etc. In the mosque were some men playing instruments.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We had lunch at the Dak Bungalow; they had cooked the vegetables very nicely.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove to Bharatapur Bird Sanctuary. On the way we saw a man on a litter, all covered with blood. When we got to the bird sanctuary, we got a little boat, and a man punted us round the marsh. He also told us what the birds were; we saw some eagles, and lots of cranes, and storks.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to Fatehpur Sikri. One of the buildings had lots of pillars, each one a different design. From the top you could see lots of things, even the stables. We then went there: on the outside there were some horse stables, inside there were the camel stables. Helena liked the Haram Sara, it was very nicely carved in all sorts of styles.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: Then we went to a bird sanctuary. The most common were painted storks (pic). The parents had yellow beaks and red heads with a long, arched neck and some pink at the tail .The wings were black underneath. The cormarants were about as big as ducks and black with a strange beak; it was curved over at the end.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went for a ride in a boat.  Spoonbill (the boat we went in) was yellow, it had two seats in the middle and one in the front.  While paddled around we saw two eagles, lots of painted storks and other birds.  We saw also some spoonbills.  The spoonbill is smaller than a stork - white with long, spatulate bill.  At mating time he wears a crest of long, narrow feathers.  Winter and juvenile plumage lack the long head feathers.  His voice is mostly silent.  (Pic - our boat).

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We spent all morning in Fatehpur Sikri.  I liked Bir Bals Palace.  It was very small with only two upper rooms.  It was very intricately carved.  It was made of red sandstone.  There were lots of niches in the wall.  In every room, one big one.  F and I played Gods by sitting in the big ones.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Drove to Sariska with the Warden.  Went for a drive - saw Nilga (antelope), Chitta (spotted deer), Sambar, Porcupine, Jackal.  Spent night in hide.  No tiger.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We saw two mongeese playing around the campsite; there was a little deer, and we stroked it. We went out on the little boat again. We saw kingfishers, egrets and one Siberian goose, as well as the things we saw yesterday.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We met the Warden of Sariska Game Reserve and we arranged to take him back to the game reserve. He said that he would take us to a hide, where there was some bait and we could watch for tigers. On the way, we saw a dog eating a carcass, with lots of vultures waiting for it to finish. When we got there, it was very late. We had already seen some deer and boar. There was a small room completely covered with a big mattress. We all lay there and watched. We saw deer drinking, but no Tigers.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We met the Ashleys - 4 kids (American)

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to look at birds again; the spoonbill was nice, especially the bit of neck with yellow and red on. It was Dad who first spotted it, a bit of skin just below the throat with yellow and red on. Also the bill itself was nice the shape and the yellow colour were beautiful (pic). Apart from spoonbill there were grey herons, purple herons, painted stork, siberion geese, pond heron, egret, ibis, snake bird, eagle, kingfisher. We were punted about in a boat through the marshes and I liked looking at the water but did not see much pond life. We drove with the warden of sariska to his reserve. He took us in the dark with a spot light. We saw antelope, spotted deer, balbul?, nilgai, porcupine, and jackals. The spotted deer stags had lovely antlers. Then we went to a hide — it was a big tower near a water hole. We waited all night but a tiger didn’t come.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We went on another boat trip that afternoon.  We found out from the boatman that the kingfisher with greenish-blue wings is called the white kingfisher.  Of course we had to photograph the painted storks nest.  We gave the warden of Sariska a lift back to Sariska where it was likely we would see a tiger because they put out a calf as bait.  We drove to a hill where we spent the night with the warden.  We saw lots of deer drinking.  (Pic)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Wild boar, porcupine, peacocks etc.  Another long drive.  No tiger.  Plenty of monkeys.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the morning, on the way back from the hide, we saw a wild boar, with 9 little babies. Ian and Viv were at the campsite. They met Collin in Delhi; he was going to Agra today.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove to the Monkey Temple. It was a Hindu temple, but lots of monkeys lived around it. We went for another drive; in the dark we saw 5 porcupines. There were 7 grown-ups, and 3 kids. We were really squashed.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We stayed at Sariska and visited the Monkey Temple.  The Monkey Temple is in a wood with two streams running into a stirred up pool.  In the temple there is a tent-like thing made of stone, under it sit a girl, Ganesh, Kali, and the sacred bull.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 39223 (11623 miles travelled).  Outside Amber.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove from Sariska to Jaipur. Just before Jaipur, we visited the palace at Amber. We rode up on an elephant! It was called Abdull, something.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove on into Jaipur. We saw lots of smart elephants and horses getting ready for weddings. We met Ian, Viv and the Ashleys at the campsite (when we at last found it). We all went out to dinner together. We saw many wedding processions. One went past the restaurant; we came out and watched. A man came and put garlands of flowers round F & H.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to the amber palace. At the bottom there were lots of ELEPHANTS! We hired one. He took us up the courtyard. The elephant was a young one, only fifteen. He had not got any tusks. The howdah was just a sort of cot shoved on the elephant. The ride was rather uncomfortable because we were squashed and the elephant swayed a lot. We went through some big gates.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: I liked it more going up the hill. In the palace there were some very nice brass gates with very interesting scenes on them. Then we went to the Hall of Mirrors. I didn’t particularly like it until a man took us inside a dark room with a lighted candle. When he moved it all the mirrors glittered in all directions and it was beautiful. They were all convex. When he opened a window I could see thousands of me’s. When we went out I saw some coloured glass reflected in the mirrors. I thought that was very nice. Then we went off to Jaipur. We visited the city palace Arms Museum. I liked some of the paintings. There were some nice demons, a little like comics — not true to life.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: There were also some nice ones, like the gods and goddesses. At the Arms Museum, ‘Welcome’ was written outside in knives and outside the exit, ‘Goodbye’. There were some daggers with very broad blades and strange handles in an H-shape which were to protect wrists. One had a little pistol on either side. Another could be opened up into 3 blades once inside the enemy. There were some clever knives with medical instruments in their handles. They had made pictures of elephants with real chain mail. There were lots of elephants in Jaipur, all dressed up for weddings and things. Also some nice city gates.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text:
We drove from Sariska to the Amber Palace.  We went up to the Palace on an Elephant!  Our Elephant was 14 years old.  In the Palace was a little set of 3 rooms, with little mirrors all over the walls.  I liked them best.  We came down on an Elephant.  We met Ian and Viv walking, they took a photo of us.
*** 23.32 ***

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 39304 (11704 miles travelled).  Tonk(?)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text:
We did some washing. While it was drying we looked at some shops. I bought things for F & H for Christmas. We came back, got the washing, and left the game park. When we arrived [at the Ranthambore Tiger Reserve, near Sawai Madhopur], it was just about dark. The Ashleys were already there. To get to the Jogi Mahal (place with loos, rooms, etc.) we had to drive under the big Banyan tree; we nearly didn’t make it, as the branches were so low. The Ashleys said it was really good for climbing.
Ashley family
Mum – Linden – lovely long hair	Megan – 11 years old
Dad – Jed – big beard	Morgan – 9 years old
Matthew – 14 years old	Mikela – 7 years old

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: In the streets of Jaipur, we saw several elephants walking in the streets, some had lovely patterns painted on them and beautiful coverings.  Two of them had beautiful howdahs with 3 seats.  There were also some horses with very bright blankets with little mirrors on; over their necks they had some braid with beads on it.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We drove across some very bumpy country roads to Sawai Mandhapor and up to the Game Reserve.  It was nearly dark when we arrived and had to drive through the enormous banyan tree.  The Ashleys were there and all the children sat round a fire under the Banyan Tree.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: 2am H feeling ill.  7.30am 103 degrees.  Shivering.  Teeth chattering.  Tummy pains, diarrohea.  ?? Doctor Dingwad(?).  Malaria.  Prescribed 2 injections of chloroquine phosphate 3cc of 5% solution. 1 immediately, 1, 24 hours later.  Also Paracetemol when fever over 100 degrees F and Erythromycin for 4 days.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: F feeling ill Noon.  4pm 103 degrees.  Gave 2 tablets chloroquine phosphate.  10pm 1 tablet.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Helena had a fever. Mum & Dad took her to a doctor in town, at the direction of Mr Fudge (Game Warden, Tiger Specialist, been to Bristol Zoo). While they were away, F said he felt tired and lay down. When they came back, H had caught malaria; she had already had one injection. They looked at F and said he must have malaria also. We rented the only room left: it was a beautiful dome, all in pink. It had a private bathroom. We put F & H to bed there.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: I went climbing in the Banyan, with “the M’s” [the four Ashley kids]. We found one place really high up, where we could sit comfortably, and called it “Falcon’s Nest”. There was another place where we had to climb up roots as if they were ropes; we called it “Monkey House”. We made our own dinner, over the fire, under the tree. It was fun.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: I felt very funny.  Mum and Dad took me to a Doctor, he said that I had Malaria and said that I had to have an injection.  We had to go to another doctor’s to make sure that I got a clean needler.  When we got back to the Sanctuary, F had also got malaria so Mummy got us a room.  It had niches in the wall, it was painted a lovely pale pink.  It had one tall window looking over the lake which had crocodiles in it.  There was a bathroom next to it.  As there was no electricity, we had kerosene lights.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: Felt ill, but slightly better.  Mr Ashley gave me my second injection.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: H - 8am temp. Normal - on way to recovery.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: F - 8am still temp 102 degrees.  1 Tablet.  Evening slightly better.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: H & F were a little better, but they still needed lots of rest. Mr Fudge’s children came over, and we went to the Ranthambore Fort. There was a little girl of 3, called Balu; we carried her most of the way (because we enjoyed it).

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We went for a ride in the jeep. We saw nilgai, chittor sambar and Indian gazelle. We also saw a baby crocodile and some monkeys. We saw one male sambar rubbing his antlers on a tree; we got very close to him. We walked down to the lake with Mr Fudge, and saw about 3 crocodiles.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: When we arrived the Ashleys were already there. There was an enormous Banyan tree: the second largest in India. They showed us round the place which was marvellous for climbing as it had put down branches as roots which we used as ropes.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: In the morning we got up early and walked down to the lake. There was a beautiful little island, some rocks, green grass and palm trees, but we did not see any crocodiles. While we walked back Morgan and I went ahead. Suddenly we heard a really loud rustling in the bushes so we ran back telling the others, “there’s a wild boar in the bushes!”.  When we got there we discovered it was only a peacock.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: When I got back I was starting to have malaria fever. H. had started one in the middle of the night. I felt ill Tuesday Wednesday and until about Thursday lunch time.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: When we went past the little village once (at the entrance to the Fort), they ushered us up onto a raised block (after removing our shoes), and made us sit down. They gave us something like breadcrumbs and sugar, on banana leaves; they plucked leaves from the tree above to eat with. Balu ate the most.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: F much better.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Helena was feeling much better, and F was a little better. The M’s and I were making a play “The Bremen Town Musicians”. We used some masks that they bought in Delhi. We took Matt up to the Fort, as he hadn’t been yet. I went with the Ashleys to wash their van. We walked downstream a bit and came to a lovely waterfall, falling into a pool. We were sitting there when we heard a low humming; we looked up and saw a huge cloud of bees. We all ran back, helter-skelter, to the van, jumped in and sped off. Matt was last, in case anyone fell over. The bees were only about two feet behind him. We had a big family BBQ, and after that we did our play. It was a great success.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We had a pink room, the lower half was white panelling with a black line round the edges and white in-sets in the black. The bathroom looked blue in the kerosene lights but green during the day. We were just above the lake which had crocodiles in it. We had a barbecue under the banyan Tree. We had goat which had been killed for us the day before. It was tasty but tough. We had potatoes, fried bananas, barbecue sauce, etc. etc. It was fun.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: I felt lots better.  I went to Antler Hall, which is a place in between lots of hanging roofs of the Banyan where the others have made a treehouse.  Whilst sweeping it out, D had found an antler in the roofs(?).  There was a little suspension bridge leading to the front door, I only once used it that day but used the back door lots.  I also went to Lookout Point.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: In the afternoon, Mum and Dad took F and I for a drive to see the wildlife.  Tiger 2 (the guide) took us to see a crocodile and as we walked back through the long grass, Daddy saw a young Sambar lying in the grass and looking at us.  When we went closer the fawn ran away.  Soon after Daddy saw another clearer(?) crocodile.  We drove on and saw a spotted deer with its baby drinking milk from it and other mothers and babies with them.  We saw a blue bull on a little track, further on there was a lake with a blue bull doe feeding in the lake.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: That night we had a barbecue under the Banyan Tree.  We had bought a whole goat, which was cut up and we cooked it on skewers.  (It was as tough as old boots.)  Mum had made some delicious barbecue sauce and Mrs Ashley made her Mexican sauce.  We had baked potatoes and onions and 4 doz chippaties.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: The other children put on a play ‘The Bremen Town Musicians’.  F and I were honoured guests, we enjoyed it thoroughly.  They used masks they had bought in Delhi - cat, dog, witch, rooster and donkey.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 39448 (11848 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We left the Ranthambore Reserve, and said goodby to Ian, Viv, and the Ashleys – we hope to see them in Bombay. We drove just about all day. We got rather lost in some places. In the late afternoon, we passed through a village. On the pavement, lots of pots were set out. We stopped. Dad said that he’d pay a maximum of 15 rupees. They were only 1 ½ rupees each. I asked about some much smaller pots. For under ½ a rupee, I bought three [PIX]

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove on until we saw a sign for a Dak Bungalow on a Game Reserve. They told us that they had about 5 tigers. Lots of people crowded round us and stared and giggled, it wasn’t very nice.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We saw a blue bird. It flitted through the air to a post. When it was flying it looked a bit like a jay, but blue-turquoise and black. When it settled it looked like a kingfisher except the back was shorter and fatter, and the head had lines going across it and looked very active. The turquoise was quite dark. On the houses there were some pictures of birds and other animals which were lots of lines inside of each other so that they got smaller and smaller. The pictures were very curved or completely straight lined .They were mainly just white lines. We drove onto a village where there were several people selling clay pots. They were very cheap. We got a big one for 1 ½ rupees. The girls got some very little ones. The girls got five pots, two glazed ones, one with a spout, two with thin necks and odd lids with a hole in, they were a rough cylinder with a rim round the middle and a hole through. [PIX]

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We started driving to Bombay.  Stopped outside J??.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 39599 (11999 miles travelled).  Jawalar(?)

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 39733 (12133 miles travelled)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove all day, apart from a lunch stop at Ujjain. We  ate in a little restaurant. I had Masala (stuffed) Dosa, and plain Dosa (pancake-like things). The road was very bad; we really jolted a lot. We are driving to Bombay; we stopped just off [the road] on a little dirt track: first time we’ve slept “out” in India.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We drove to Bombay but did not reach it on the way. We gave away some shells.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: We drove all day but stopped for lunch at Ujjain.  We had lunch in a pleasant Hotel restaurant.  I was ordered an omelette but it was not so another was ordered.  We were waiting to cross a bridge - some children came - we gave them some shells which we had gathered in the Caspian.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 39872 (12272 miles travelled).  Shirpur

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 39997 (12397 miles travelled).  Near Nasik

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 40157 (12557 miles travelled).  Bombay

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove on, and at last entered Bombay at 4pm. As we had been getting closer and closer, the climate had been getting warmer and warmer. When we actually entered Bombay it was very hot and sticky. We drove around looking for somewhere to camp. We met some nuns, who invited us to their convent if we couldn’t find anywhere else.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Saw Sunder(?). ?? to ??  Space definitely booked.  Went to WIAA.  Can’t insure.  Can’t clear without one of us, unless lockable Customs shed.  Boat unlikely to arrive Bombay before 31.  Prob NOT Brisbane.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We stayed the night at the convent: H, F & I slept there. Our beds had mosquito netting over them, and we had a private toilet and shower. When we woke up, they took us to breakfast. We had porridge, then omelettes and Dal. All day we went round offices; it was very hot. At lunch I cut my thumb when I was peeling carrots; it bled a lot.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: There are lots of palm trees lining the roads, or in gardens, etc. Some of them have coconuts growing in them. There were lots of people selling big, green, fresh coconuts, so we bought one. The man cut off the top and gave us a straw; the coconut was full of milk. When we’d drunk it all, the man scraped out the flesh: it was all rubbery.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We stayed at the convent again, the nuns were very kind. Sister Hilary looked after us. As soon as we were ready, we went to see Ratty’s mum (Mrs Engineer). She had a lovely big, cool flat. She and Mum and Dad went to see some more people about shipping Fred. Us kids stayed at the flat, reading and munching crisps (chili!). She then took us out to lunch (because her cook had flu). We went to a completely vegetarian restaurant. We all ordered Thali meals except Helena, who had cheese on toast. We had soup, and then the Thali meal, and then fruit salad. Unfortunately, the Thali was too hot for me. [The Thali meal had little bowls of dal and rice, puffed up chapatties, coleslaw salad, and a little cabbage roll] [PIC] On the tray was also yoghurt and a very sweet rice pudding.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: It was our last night at the convent, so in the morning we said good-bye, and packed everything back in Fred. We shopped round the emporiums; first we left a message in the PO for the Ashleys. When we came back to Fred, after shopping, there was a little note from the Ashleys!

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove to their hotel, and there they were. We talked a bit, and then all the children came with us to the cinema. What we saw was a documentary on India, and it was awful! After the film, we had to go to Jehu beach. The Ashleys weren’t coming; we’ll probably never see them again. Jehu beach was very built up and not very nice. Us kids went swimming.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 40233 (12633 miles travelled).  Outside Bombay

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We made a big sandcastle, with a running water moat, and big, high walls, but the sea came and surrounded and overpowered it. Then we went swimming. After we had showered and dried we went out hoping to get a camel ride, but we couldn't find one.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We left, and after a lot of wrong directions left Bombay, to go to Ajanta and Ellora. We found a PW&H view point. There weren’t any buildings, just benches in little terraced gardens. It was all very wild. We cooked outside on the petrol stove, it made a lot of noise. F & H found a big insect, drowned, in a pool. I counted 24 mosquito bites below one knee.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 40334 (12734 miles travelled).  Outside Nasik

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Petrol from jerry can Mileage = 40507 (12907 miles travelled).  20 km from Ajanta

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We got all ready, but Fred wouldn’t start. In the end, Dad had to clean out all the spark plugs. At last we got going again; the car coughed a lot, but kept going. In the afternoon we stopped in Nasik to do our Christmas shopping. We had great fun. We bought 4 dozen bananas, etc.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We drove through Ellora village, but decided to go on to Ajanta, as the Ashleys told us the Forest Rest House was better there. At last we saw a sign to the rest house; we drove up and parked. We went into the dining room, and there were an English lady and gentleman (Mary & Philip). They were very nice. We settled to stay here. All the water is lugged up from the quickly drying-up river; the loos are horrible.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We invited P&M to have lunch with us. There was also a very interesting Swiss-German Ethnolinguist, who could speak Hindi, but he couldn’t come. We had fried ham and bananas and mashed potatoes, then a big fruit salad and sweetened condensed milk. We walked up to the stalls at Ajanta caves. There were some beautiful stones there. F bought me 3 necklaces.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: In the morning, we all told each other what we were giving them.  We invited some English called Philip and Mary to lunch.  We had a whole pressure cooker full of fruit salad.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 40588 (12988 miles travelled).  Anvangabad(?)

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We went to Ajanta caves. We had to do lots of climbing up and down, but there were some beautiful carvings. We went and bought some stones. I bought an ordinary pebble, but it opened and was hollow, with crystals round the inside. We gave P&M a lift to Aurangabad, and then went on to Ellora. We are waiting for food at the restaurant. PS It was delicious.

entries.speaker: F
entries.text: We went to the caves.  They were Buddhist.  There were lots of people sitting on serpents with lots of heads.  The Buddhas sat on a seat with two deer carved on it.  There were some nice paintings but there was such a queue, we didn’t go in.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Mileage = 40700 (13100 miles travelled).  Ahamed Nagar.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Camped wild, near Poone

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We went to visit the Hindu caves at Ellora first. There had been a big thing of rock, and they had carved down and made lots of temples, all out of the one piece of rock. [PIC] There were some super carvings.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We saw a few Buddhist temples as well, but we’ve seen so many that we decided to leave some of them out. We also saw the Jain temple, but we were getting so tired that we didn’t take much in.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Ajanta caves looked very new, because the rock was so hard that it had hardly weathered at all. The carvings were mainly of gods, and little fat men, who we think were devils. The whole thing had been painted, but it was mostly bare rock that we saw. There were a few better preserved paintings, but even these were very dim and cracked.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: The Ellora temples were much less like caves [than the Ajanta ones], although they also were carved out of a rock face. The carvings were similar to those of Ajanta, and were fairly clear, but most of the paintings had gone.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We left Ellora, because Fred wasn’t working properly, and we wanted a good start. He went quite well, but we couldn’t find a campsite. At last we found a little motorable road, and pulled off.

entries.speaker: H
entries.text: From Ajanta, we drove to Ellora and spent the night in a Hotel with a shop and ate out.  In the morning, we visited the Hindu caves.  The first one we went into was very big with a large temple in the centre.  (The temple filled up most of the cave.)  The cave itself was not really an actual cave because it had not got a roof covering everything.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We woke up and drove to Poona, which is a hill resort near Bombay. We drove straight through. The road was very bad and Fred wasn’t working well. At last we got to Bombay at about 4:30pm. It was hot, but not as bad as when we came before. We stayed at the Sea Palace Hotel, as Mrs Engineer isn’t expecting us til tomorrow. There are lots of rats scurrying about. The next morning we saw two lovely sailing ships; one had 4 and one had 5 sails.[PIC]  It was very interesting, but misty, so it looked a bit spooky.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: At about 9:00am we drove to a garage. We left Dad there and went to walk about, looking at shops etc. First they were all shut, but at about 10:00 they began to open. We saw a snake charmer; the cobra was a bit sleepy though. [PIC] We also saw a lady beating a drum. Her children were performing: going through hoops together and things. We had lunch at the Ideal Restaurant, but before we got a chance to order any more, the waiter brought the fennel seeds and finger bowls, so we went to another restaurant. It was very funny.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Antia says ship not expected until 2nd or 3rd & will ring on Sat.  May not load until 9th.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: From the garage, we went on to Mrs Nargis Engineer’s. In the morning we lay in a bit. There are lots of Agatha Christie books.

entries.speaker: G/M
entries.text: Cancelled plan and rebooked to Bangkok.  Requested for Singapore and Brisbane.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Staying with Mrs Engineer, reading and pottering round Bombay.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: F, H & I went shopping with Nargis; she bought H & I some perfume, and F a wooden box. She took us to a restaurant for lunch. She and I had “Temptation”; it was delicious, but had too much mustard. On the 6th I am going to a wedding with Nargis. I tried on a blouse of Nina’s. Mum took it in a bit. I’m borrowing a silk sari.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We went for a walk at the sea, to the Aquarium. Mum had a sore throat, so we left her at home with Nargis. We saw garfish, crabs and another kind of fish; the aquarium had some baby sharks. Mum picked us up and we went to India Gate. While we were parking the car, F & H saw a mongoose eating a snake. It was a special show thing.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: I bought a swim-suit set at the beach: a bikini, gathered skirt, bag, and headband. They are printed Indian cotton. [PIC] I also got some shoes at the Taj. They are hard brown leather with soft blue leather for the straps, etc. [PIC]

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: At night we went to the lunar park; there was an exhibition of Indian handicrafts there.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: F, H & I went to the Oberoi Sheraton Hotel, to swim. I wore my new set. The water was very cold, so we just lay in the sun. The sun wasn’t very hot either, and there was a strong breeze blowing. The pool was quite high, so we had an interesting view of Bombay. [PIC]

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: I heard some strange music. I looked out of the flat window, and there were two enormous pythons, at least 6 feet long. The man was playing to them, and also to a sleepy looking cobra in a basket. The pythons were moving slowly along the ground, and every now and then the man would stop and drag them back to him.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: A big procession is just passing, with a band and some people holding a canopy, but no-one seems to be underneath it. Nargis said that she would give me a sari if I could tie it. I could, and she's given me a beautiful white silk one, with red embroidery on it.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: In the morning, I went to the hairdresser with Mum and Nargis. They washed, and then cut my hair (like this – no, can’t draw it). I was very careful not to get it out of shape.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: At last, evening came and Nargis and I got dressed. I was borrowing an embroidered white silk sari. When we got there, the ceremony had just been performed, and the bride and groom had come out of the Fire Temple and were sitting on a large dais being congratulated by long lines of friends and relations. There was a band and singer (a lady) on the left. We sat around talking. The bride and groom got off the dais, and the first sitting of dinner was announced. We decided that we’d go for the second sitting. [PIC]

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We sat down at one of the long thin tables; the table cloth was whipped away, and a fresh one put on. We were each given 2/3 banana leaves, spread in front of us, and a glass. Then the food came round and was set on our leaves; there was bread, wafers, fish, chicken, sweets and ice cream – as much as you could eat. I was soon full.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: At the end, they came around wrapping up our banana leaves, in which were the left-overs – for the beggars. The whole place was decorated with flowers; there were at least 2000 people there. The grounds were very big.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We visited the dock, but couldn’t get in without a pass.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We got up at 7:30am and had breakfast, then we walked to India Gate to catch a ferry to go to Elephanta Island. As we chugged along, we saw some enormous ships carrying oil, cargo – and one battle ship with two helicopters on it. There are also some Lanteen boats; one took us from our ferry to the island. There were Hindu caves, dedicated to Lord Shiva. We had a good guide.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text:
Recipe - Nilgiri Pancakes (6 pancakes) - courtesy of Narghish (Mrs Engineer)
1 egg
¼ cup powdered sugar
Milk as required
1 cup flour
Salt to taste
Ghee for frying
Mix the egg and flour in a bowl.  Add the milk and stir til the batter is of the consistency of cream.  Add salt.  Melt the ghee in a deep pan, and heat the pancake gadget in it.  Dip the gadget half way into the batter and hold in the ghee to fry.  When it browns slightly, shake the gadget to remove the pancake, then fry the pancake til it is crisp.  Remove from the pan and sprinkle with powdered sugar.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Last night we took Nargis out to dinner at “Gaylords”. There was a band, and F & H, and Mum and Dad danced. We had a lovely time. Nargis and I went to collect my “choli” (sari blouse) which was being made at her tailor. It was a little tight, so we arranged to come back later.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Mum and Dad came with the good news that Fred was on the ship, happily sailing out of the harbour. We got my choli; I put it on with my new petticoat, and then wrapped my sari round. The colours matched very well.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: Dad finished reading Kim. The traffic is terribly noisy, and it’s difficult to sleep.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We woke and started packing, and getting sorted out for the journey. We said thank-you to Nargis, and drove to the station. It was a typical main station; smaller, but with double the amount of people. We got on the train, the seats were like reclining aircraft seats, with little tables. They were very uncomfortable. They served us afternoon tea: biscuits, tea, and a hot little patty. There was a little library; we got out three books: one Agatha Christie, one Biggles, and one big book of comics. We had dinner: there was rice, curry and vegetables, curds and ice cream. It was very difficult to sleep.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: When we woke up, there was a beautiful sunset. For breakfast we had 2 boiled eggs, 2 buttered toast, and coffee. We arrived at Delhi; we couldn’t find Prenna, but we rang the house and she was there; she told us to go to the YMCA. We squeezed in five beds to one room. We went to the post office. For me, there was only 1 letter, from Georgina. We went to Prenna’s house. Nippy was there. We had lunch and sat around talking. Ranjit came home and then Mrs Pai came. We went shopping, and Mum bought a lovely furry shawl. We came back and had dinner; at last we went back to the YMCA; we were very tired.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We had breakfast at the YMCA; it took ages. Then we went shopping with Prenna, Mrs Pai and Nippy. We got a shawl for me, not a furry one, it’s  lovely bright red and should go with my sari. We went to pick up F, H & Dad in Jan Path, unfortunately, the shop they wanted to see was closed for some minor festival.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We picked up our things from the YMCA and taxied to the airport. After the first formalities, we sat down and had a snack-lunch, then went to be searched. At last, we got in the plane. All the girls got a beautiful little bouquet of orchids.

entries.speaker: D
entries.text: We stopped at Dacca for a while. Before, we had tea; after, dinner.
